title: Delegated provisioning: onboarding approvals, safety checks, and utilization telemetry
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: As Redwood scales Dedicated reservations we get frequent manual handoffs for capacity approvals, conservative safety buffers that waste committed GPU hours, and poor visibility into early-stage under/over-provisioning. This results in slow onboarding, frustrated customers, and inefficient utilization.

Objective: Define and ship a delegated provisioning workflow that: 1) allows authorized customer ops or SRE contacts to self-approve lower-risk requests; 2) codifies safety checks and automatic guardrails for initial reservation sizing; and 3) surfaces utilization telemetry and rollback triggers in the Console so the onboarding team can recover capacity or re-negotiate commitments quickly.

Scope: This ticket covers product requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and integrations with the autoscale policy engine and fleet controls. Engineering work to implement APIs and runtime changes will be tracked as dependent ENG tickets. Not in scope: pricing model changes, contract/legal language changes (handled by CS/legal separately).
acceptance_criteria: Delegated-approver role can be attached to a customer account in the Console and grants the ability to approve requests up to a configurable throughput and duration limit
Provisioning request form includes recommended sizing and safety buffer generated by the estimator service (inputs: historical usage, burst profile, target SLOs)
Onboarding safety checks run pre-approval and flag risk levels (low/medium/high) with automated guardrail suggestions (e.g., lower initial throughput, probation window)
Autoscale policies can be attached to new reservations with default 'probation' parameters that limit burst and define telemetry collection windows
Console shows a dedicated telemetry panel for new reservations with 1h/24h/7d utilization, rolling latency percentiles, and a 'health' widget that maps to rollback triggers
Audit log entries are created for every approval action with approver identity, policy snapshot, and estimated commit cost
Integration tests cover delegated flow, policy attachment, telemetry pipeline, and audit logging
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal pilot): 2 customers, enable delegated approvals with conservative limits and manual ops shadowing (2 weeks)
Phase 1 (beta): expand to up to 10 customers, enable probation autoscale policy and telemetry dashboards, collect feedback (4 weeks)
Phase 2 (general availability): open delegated approvals to all eligible accounts with role validation + SSO; enable auto-enforcement of safety checks
Fallback: ability to revoke delegated role and revert to manual approval; automatic rollback if telemetry triggers sustained breach of rollback policy
risks: Delegated approvers could approve oversized reservations leading to capacity shortages for other customers
Telemetry lag or missing signals could cause false negatives on rollback triggers
Complexity in policy translation between Console UI defaults and runtime autoscale engine
Audit or RBAC edge cases could expose control plane surfaces if misconfigured
mitigations: Hard limits on delegated approvals configurable per-customer, enforced server-side
Require a 48-hour probation with conservative autoscale caps for all delegated-approved reservations
Implement server-side policy schema validation and preflight simulation before commit
Add mandatory SSO verification for delegated approver creation and periodic revalidation
Instrument telemetry pipeline with synthetic canaries and alerting for ingestion lag
